text: 70-year-old woman. The patient presents with sudden episodes of dizziness that are position dependent. text: The positive Dix-Hallpike maneuver confirms Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). I will now perform the Epley maneuver to reposition the displaced otoconia in your right ear. Please remain still as I guide your head through the specific positions to relieve your symptoms.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical or surgical history. No history of Meniere's disease, vestibular neuritis, or labyrinthitis. Social history: Retired school teacher. Lives alone. Non-smoker, occasional wine. Enjoys light gardening.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the Dix-Hallpike test was positive for horizontal nystagmus, which indicates a horizontal canal variant, the Epley maneuver is not the correct treatment. I will now perform the Lempert roll maneuver to treat your horizontal canal BPPV. Please lie flat on your back as I guide your head through the rotation sequence.
